equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect daily for broken or loose parts; red-tag and replace defects

equipment_rows.training: Authorized to use; trained per manufacturer
equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect before each use; guards in place; red-tag defects
Inspect before each use; test GFCI; no tape repairs

equipment_rows.equipment: Standard PPE (hard hat, safety glasses, cut-resistant gloves, hi-vis vest, work boots)
equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect daily; replace damaged PPE immediately

competent_persons.activity: Supervise safety on the job site

steps.name: Site-specific training and orientation
hazards: Workers untrained on site hazards or the task
controls: Complete the GC site orientation before starting work
Review this JHA with the crew and collect signatures before work begins
Review again when new crew members join
Stop and amend the JHA with the Safety Department if the scope or conditions change

steps.name: Daily pre-task plan
steps.name_es: Plan diario antes de la tarea
hazards: Crews and trades working without a shared plan
controls: Foreman reviews the day's tasks, hazards, and controls with the crew before starting
Coordinate work areas and sequencing with other trades and the GC superintendent
Document the huddle per company and GC requirements
Anyone can stop work for an unsafe condition

steps.name: Wear required PPE
steps.name_es: Usar el equipo de protección personal requerido
hazards: Head, eye, hand, or foot injury
controls: Hard hat, safety glasses, cut-resistant gloves, hi-vis vest, and work boots at all times
Hearing protection when noise exceeds 85 dBA
Goggles or face shield when the task or SDS requires
No loose clothing or jewelry that can snag
Replace damaged PPE immediately

steps.name: Enter the site and walk the work area
steps.name_es: Entrar al sitio y recorrer el área de trabajo
controls: Walk the route and work area at the start of each shift
Keep a clear path of travel and clear exits
Report uncovered openings or missing guardrails to the GC; do not work until protected
Never remove hole covers or guardrails
Stay clear of overhead work, pinch points, and moving equipment

steps.name: Receive and store materials
hazards: Struck by delivery vehicles or forklifts
controls: Stay clear of moving equipment and heed backup alarms
Stack material stable, level, and at a safe height
Stage close to the point of use in approved laydown areas
Keep material away from floor openings and edges
Store flammables only in approved storage

steps.name: Lift, carry, and move materials
controls: Team lift heavy or awkward loads
Use carts, dollies, and handling aids whenever possible
Balance the load and watch your path
Never move material above other workers
Seal paint and liquids before moving
Do not stand in front of or above a wall or floor opening while stocking

steps.name: Inspect tools before use
controls: Inspect before each use; tag and remove defective tools from the site
Never remove, bypass, or modify guards or safety devices
Use tools only as intended and per the manufacturer
GFCI protection on every circuit serving tools

steps.name: Extension cords and temporary power
controls: Hard- or extra-hard-usage cords; factory-assembled sets where possible
No cords with cuts, worn insulation, exposed conductors, or missing ground prongs
No tape repairs; send damaged cords for repair or disposal
GFCI on every cord
Elevate cords or route them out of walkways and doorways

steps.name: Work around other trades
hazards: Dust and fumes from other work
controls: Ear plugs from 85 to 115 dBA; plugs and muffs above 115 dBA
Coordinate sequencing with the GC to avoid stacked trades
Keep unprotected workers out of areas where coatings give off hazardous fumes
Barricade your work area when others pass through

steps.name: Housekeeping and cleanup
controls: Clean as you go and at the end of each shift
Store equipment out of travel paths; stack material in the laydown area
Sweeping compound or HEPA vacuum; no dry sweeping or compressed air on dust
Blades and sharps in a closed container

steps.name: Emergency response and first aid
steps.name_es: Respuesta a emergencias y primeros auxilios
hazards: Delayed response to an injury or fire
controls: Crew knows the site address, emergency contacts, and muster point
First aid kit and a trained person on site
Crew knows where fire extinguishers are
Report every injury and near miss to the foreman immediately

equipment_rows.inspection: Check daily; replace damaged signs
Check edges are taped down each shift
Inspect cords and filters before use

steps.name: Coordinate with tenant and building
steps.name_es: Coordinar con el inquilino y el edificio
controls: Schedule with the building manager; after-hours for high-odor or disruptive work
Post notice to occupants before work starts
Confirm access, elevator use, and loading dock times
Know the building's emergency procedures and alarm signals

steps.name: Isolate and barricade the work area
steps.name_es: Aislar y delimitar el área de trabajo
hazards: Occupants contacting wet paint, ladders, or tools
controls: Barricade and sign the work area
Keep exits, corridors, and fire equipment clear at all times
Never leave ladders, lifts, or open containers unattended
Wet paint signs until dry

steps.name: Control odors, dust, and vapors
hazards: Vapors or dust migrating into occupied areas and HVAC
controls: Low- or zero-VOC products where specified
Coordinate HVAC shutdown or return-air protection with the building engineer
Ventilate to the exterior; negative air where required
HEPA vacuum cleanup; no dry sweeping

steps.name: Protect finishes and fire systems
steps.name_es: Proteger acabados y sistemas contra incendios
hazards: Covered smoke detectors or sprinklers left disabled
controls: Mask and cover furniture and finishes
Cover smoke detectors only with building approval; uncover at end of shift
Never paint sprinkler heads or fire devices

steps.name: Secure materials at end of shift
steps.name_es: Asegurar materiales al final del turno
controls: Close containers and lock up materials
Remove or secure ladders and lifts
Leave the area clean and walkable

equipment_rows.inspection: Daily
Check daily
Verify owner lockout before each task

competent_persons.activity: Supervise safety on the job site

steps.name: Owner orientation and permits
controls: Complete the owner's safety orientation before starting
Obtain required permits (hot work, lift, confined space, line break)
Follow owner PPE rules, which may exceed ours
Know the facility alarm signals and muster point

steps.name: Work near operating equipment
steps.name_es: Trabajar cerca de equipo en operación
controls: Owner-performed lockout before work on or near equipment; verify zero energy
Never operate owner equipment or valves
Keep clear of moving conveyors, robots, and machinery
Treat pipes and surfaces as hot until confirmed

steps.name: Forklift and vehicle traffic
controls: Hi-vis vests at all times
Barricade the work zone; use a spotter near traffic lanes
Coordinate traffic routes and work hours with the facility
Make eye contact with operators before crossing

steps.name: Protect product and equipment
hazards: Overspray or dust on product and equipment
controls: Mask and cover equipment below and around work
Coordinate shutdowns and area turnover with the facility
No spraying near air intakes without approval

steps.name: Housekeeping and egress
controls: Keep aisles, exits, and fire equipment clear
Stage materials only in approved areas

equipment_rows.equipment: Drinking water (at least 1 qt per worker per hour)
equipment_rows.inspection: Check supply at start of shift and through the day
In place before temperatures exceed 80°F
Inspect cords before use

steps.name: Provide water, shade, and rest
controls: Fresh, cool water available all shift, close to the work
Shade or cool-down area when temperatures exceed 80°F (outdoors) or per the indoor heat plan
Encourage preventative cool-down breaks; never discourage breaks
High-heat procedures above 95°F: observation, reminders, and crew check-ins

steps.name: Acclimatize and monitor the crew
hazards: New or returning workers at higher risk
controls: Close observation of new workers during their first 14 days
Buddy system during high heat
Schedule the heaviest work for cooler hours where possible

steps.name: Respond to heat illness symptoms
steps.name_es: Responder a síntomas de enfermedad por calor
controls: Crew knows the signs: dizziness, confusion, heavy or no sweating, nausea
Move the worker to shade and begin cooling; do not leave them alone
Call 911 for confusion, collapse, or no improvement
Crew knows the site address and directions for emergency services

equipment_rows.inspection: Doors close and latch; labeled; inspected weekly
Inspect lids and flame arrestors before use
Charged, tagged, and accessible; inspected monthly

steps.name: Store flammable and combustible liquids
controls: Store in approved cabinets or a designated storage area approved by the GC
No more than 25 gal of flammable liquids in a room outside approved cabinets
Never store in exits, stairways, or near ignition sources
Keep containers closed and labeled
No smoking signs posted; extinguisher at the storage area

steps.name: Dispense and transfer
controls: Transfer only in ventilated areas away from ignition sources
Bond and ground metal containers during transfer
Use approved safety cans for portable quantities
Keep absorbent on hand

steps.name: Waste, rags, and empty containers
controls: Oily and solvent rags in a closed metal can; empty daily
Label and store waste per project and local requirements
Never pour solvents or paint into drains

equipment_rows.training: Trained in use; calibrated per manufacturer
equipment_rows.inspection: Bump test before each use
Inspect before use
Inspect before each use

competent_persons.activity: Confined space evaluation and entry supervision

steps.name: Evaluate the space
hazards: Entering a permit-required space without controls
controls: No entry into any tank, pit, vault, or enclosed space until evaluated by a competent person
Permit-required spaces entered only under a written permit program
If the owner or GC controls the space, follow their permit and coordinate entry

steps.name: Test and ventilate the atmosphere
hazards: Flammable or toxic vapors from coatings
controls: Test oxygen, flammability, and toxics before entry and continuously during work
Continuous forced-air ventilation while coating
Only products reviewed for confined-space use (check SDS)
Supplied-air respirator where required by the permit or SDS

steps.name: Entry, attendant, and rescue
controls: Trained attendant outside at all times with communication to entrants
Rescue plan and equipment in place before entry
Never enter to rescue without proper equipment; call rescue services

equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect for defects before each use; red-tag defects

competent_persons.note: Inspected by user before each use

steps.name: Select the right ladder
hazards: Overreaching from a ladder that is too short
controls: Type I or IA duty rating; no Type III (light duty) ladders
Fiberglass when working near electrical
Tall enough to work without standing on the top step or the top 3 rungs
Never exceed the duty rating (worker plus tools and material)

steps.name: Inspect the ladder
controls: Inspect rails, rungs, feet, spreaders, and locks before each use
Keep ladders clean of paint, oil, and mud
Red-tag and remove defective ladders until repaired or replaced

steps.name: Set up the ladder
hazards: Struck by people, doors, or vehicles
controls: Firm, level footing; never on boxes, buckets, or loose material
Stepladders fully open and locked; never lean a closed stepladder
Extension ladders at 4:1, extended 36 in. above the landing, secured top and bottom
Not in front of a door unless it is locked, blocked, or guarded
Barricade or post a helper in traffic areas
At least 10 ft from overhead power lines

steps.name: Climb and work from the ladder
steps.name_es: Subir y trabajar desde la escalera
controls: Face the ladder and keep 3 points of contact while climbing
Carry tools in a pouch or raise them with a line
Keep your belt buckle between the rails; move the ladder instead of overreaching
Do not stand on the top step, top cap, or top 3 rungs of an extension ladder
Do not straddle to another object or push and pull hard enough to shift the ladder
One person on the ladder at a time

equipment_rows.training: Scaffold certification required for all users; documentation provided
equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect on delivery and before each shift by a competent person; green tag; red-tag defects

competent_persons.note: Inspected by user before each use

steps.name: Inspect and tag
controls: Competent person inspects before each shift; initial and date the green tag
Red-tag missing, damaged, or mismatched parts until repaired
Only trained users on the scaffold

steps.name: Set up the scaffold
controls: All diagonal and horizontal bracing in place; scaffold square
Guardrails (top rail about 42 in. plus midrail) and full-width planking
Outriggers where the height-to-base ratio requires
Check the floor for openings, slopes, cords, and debris before setup

steps.name: Work from the platform
controls: Wheels locked and scaffold immobilized while working
Climb only the built-in ladder or access frame; never the cross braces
No ladders, buckets, or planks on the platform to gain height
Stay within the rated load
Keep the area below clear; toeboards or barricades where others pass

steps.name: Move the scaffold
controls: Clear the path and check overhead before moving
Push at or near the base; never pull from the platform
Riders only as allowed under T8 §1646(i)–(j); otherwise no one on the platform while moving
Secure tools and materials before moving

equipment_rows.training: Scaffold user training; erectors trained under a competent person
equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect before each shift by a competent person; tagged

competent_persons.note: Inspected by user before each use

steps.name: Erect or accept the scaffold
controls: Erect, alter, or dismantle only under a competent person
Use a GC or scaffold-contractor scaffold only after it is inspected and tagged
Base plates and mudsills on firm footing; ties per height requirements
Fully planked with gaps no more than 1 in.; planks overlap at least 12 in.

steps.name: Access the scaffold
controls: Use built-in ladders or stair towers
Never climb cross braces
3 points of contact; raise tools with a line or bucket

steps.name: Work on the scaffold
controls: Top rail 42 in. ±3 in., midrail, and toeboards at least 3.5 in.
Personal fall arrest where guardrails are not feasible
Tether tools; bag or bucket materials up and down
No horseplay; keep platforms clear of debris and spilled paint

steps.name: Weather and end of shift
controls: No work in high wind or storms
Clear water, paint, and debris from platforms before use

equipment_rows.training: Scissor lift certification required for all operators; documentation provided
equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect on delivery and before each shift; green tag; red-tag defects until repaired

steps.name: Pre-use inspection
controls: Trained and authorized operators only; manual on board
Test controls, emergency stop, and emergency lowering before each shift
Guardrails, gate, and brakes in working condition
Red-tag any lift with defects until repaired

steps.name: Check the work area
hazards: Tip-over from holes, slopes, or drop-offs
controls: Firm, level surface free of holes, debris, and cords
Confirm the floor or deck can carry the lift
At least 10 ft from power lines
Barricade the area below

steps.name: Work from the platform
controls: Gate closed; feet on the platform floor; never stand or sit on the rails
Tie off to the manufacturer anchor when required by the manufacturer or company
Do not exceed the load rating
Keep work within easy reach; lower and reposition instead of leaning out
Tether tools; keep the area below clear

steps.name: Drive and position the lift
controls: Do not drive elevated unless the manufacturer allows it and the path is checked
Watch overhead and to the sides while elevating
Hands inside the platform while traveling
Spotter in tight areas and near other workers

equipment_rows.training: Boom lift certification required for all operators; documentation provided
equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect on delivery and before each shift; green tag; red-tag defects
Inspect before each use; red-tag defects

competent_persons.activity: Fall protection supervision / inspection of fall protection equipment
competent_persons.note: Inspected by user before each use

steps.name: Pre-use inspection
controls: Trained and authorized operators only; manual on board
Test ground and platform controls, emergency stop, and emergency lowering
Inspect tires, outriggers, hydraulics, and guardrails
Red-tag any lift with defects until repaired

steps.name: Set up and travel
hazards: Tip-over on slopes, soft ground, or openings
controls: Check ground conditions and slope limits; use a spotter
Stay at least 10 ft from power lines
Travel with the boom lowered and retracted where required
Barricade the swing and work area

steps.name: Work from the basket
hazards: Fall or ejection from the basket
controls: Full-body harness and lanyard tied to the basket anchor at all times
Feet on the basket floor; never climb or sit on the rails
Watch overhead clearance while elevating and slewing
Do not exceed the load rating; tether tools; keep the area below clear

equipment_rows.training: Trained in donning and use before starting work
equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect before each use; SRL-LE (ANSI Z359.14) for leading edge; red-tag defects

competent_persons.activity: Fall protection supervision / inspection of fall protection equipment
competent_persons.note: Inspected by user before each use

steps.name: Identify openings and edges
hazards: Falls through openings or from edges
controls: Walk the area and identify openings, shafts, skylights, and edges 6 ft or more above a lower level
Report missing covers or guardrails to the GC; do not work until protected
Never remove covers or rails; if removal is needed, get GC approval and protect the opening

steps.name: Work near unprotected edges
steps.name_es: Trabajar cerca de bordes sin protección
hazards: Falls causing serious injury or death
controls: Guardrail, safety net, or personal fall arrest at 6 ft or more
Fall arrest limits arresting force to 1,800 lb, free fall to 6 ft, and deceleration to 3.5 ft, with no contact with a lower level
Anchors rated 5,000 lb per worker or designed by a qualified person
SRL-LE rated for leading edge (ANSI Z359.14) where lines cross an edge
Inspect equipment before each use; rescue plan in place

steps.name: Prevent dropped objects
hazards: Tools or material falling on workers below
controls: Tether tools; toeboards or debris nets at edges
Barricade the area below
Never throw material down

equipment_rows.training: Trained by supervisor before use; authorized to use
equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect daily for damaged parts, hoses, and cords; tip guard in place; tag and replace defects

equipment_rows.training: Medical clearance, fit test, and training on use and maintenance
equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect before each use; replace filters on mfr. schedule; clean daily; store sealed
Inspect poles and extensions for damage
Charged, tagged, and within reach of spray areas

competent_persons.activity: Evaluate silica exposures and implement exposure control plan
competent_persons.note: If sanding or cutting silica-containing materials

steps.name: Review SDS and product requirements
steps.name_es: Revisar SDS y requisitos del producto
controls: Read the SDS for every product before use
Wear the PPE and respirator the SDS requires
Keep SDS accessible on site
Label every secondary container

steps.name: Open cans and mix paint
controls: Gloves; keep tool edges pointed away from the body
Safety glasses; goggles for splash-prone mixing
Mix on a level surface in a ventilated area; mixer at low speed
Close containers when not in use

steps.name: Prepare surfaces (patch, sand, clean)
hazards: Dust from sanding compound and existing coatings
controls: Vacuum-attached sanders or wet methods
N95 available for voluntary use; respirator where the silica plan or SDS requires
Confirm existing coatings are not lead or asbestos before sanding; if unknown, stop and notify the PM
Safety glasses; HEPA vacuum cleanup

steps.name: Mask and protect
controls: Retractable blades and cut-resistant gloves
Tape down sheeting edges
Do not cover exits, fire alarm devices, or sprinkler heads without GC approval; uncover at the end of the task

steps.name: Apply by brush and roller
hazards: Strain from repetitive or awkward reaching
controls: Safety glasses and gloves
Ventilate the work area
Stretch before starting; use extension poles; rotate tasks
Position the body to avoid awkward reaching

steps.name: Set up the airless sprayer
steps.name_es: Instalar la máquina de pintar sin aire
controls: Never use a gun without a tip guard; confirm the trigger lock works
Inspect hose, fittings, and gauge; replace damaged hose
Ground the pump; GFCI on the cord
Route hoses out of walkways

steps.name: Spray with an airless
controls: Never point the gun at anyone; trigger lock on when not spraying
Unplug and relieve pressure before a tip change, cleaning, or repair
Never clear a clogged tip with a finger or look into it
Replace a leaking hose; never hold a rag over a leak
Respirator per the written program and SDS; goggles
Mask off and ventilate
Get emergency care right away for any injection injury, even if it looks minor

steps.name: Control ignition sources and ventilation
steps.name_es: Controlar fuentes de ignición y ventilación
controls: No smoking, open flame, or hot work in spray areas
Extinguisher within reach
Ventilate to keep vapors low; explosion-proof fans when spraying solvent products
Bond and ground containers when transferring flammables
Only one day's supply of flammables in the work area

steps.name: Caulk and apply sealants
controls: Read the SDS; gloves per the SDS
Ventilate the work area
Cut tubes away from the body

steps.name: Clean up paint spills
controls: Contain with absorbent; keep out of drains
PPE for the product
Bag or drum waste and dispose per project and local rules
Report large spills to the foreman and GC

steps.name: Clean brushes, rollers, and sprayer
controls: Flush at low pressure with the tip removed; ground the gun to the metal pail
Wash out only in approved areas; never in storm drains
Oily and solvent rags in a closed metal can; empty daily
Wash hands and exposed skin when finished

equipment_rows.training: Trained in use; used only where company and GC allow
equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect straps, springs, and adjustments before each use
Check hoses and HEPA filter before use
Inspect paddle, cord, and trigger before use

competent_persons.activity: Evaluate silica exposures and implement exposure control plan

steps.name: Mix joint compound
hazards: Strain or wrist injury from mixer torque
controls: Use premixed compound where possible
Add powder slowly; mix at low speed
Brace the mixer with both hands
Safety glasses; N95 available for voluntary use

steps.name: Tape, bed, and skim
hazards: Falls from stilts, benches, or ladders
controls: Stilts only where allowed, on clean, level floors free of cords and debris
Benches and planks used within their rating; guardrails where required by height
Follow ladder and scaffold templates for work at height
Rotate tasks and stretch

steps.name: Sand
controls: Vacuum-attached sanders with HEPA or wet sponge sanding
Respirator where the silica plan or SDS requires; N95 for voluntary use otherwise
Safety glasses
HEPA vacuum cleanup; no dry sweeping or compressed air

equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect hose, wand, trigger, and fittings daily; GFCI on electric units

steps.name: Set up the washer
controls: Gas units outdoors only, exhaust away from doors, windows, and air intakes
GFCI on electric units; keep connections dry
Let the engine cool before refueling; refuel with the engine off

steps.name: Wash surfaces
controls: Never point the wand at anyone; use the widest tip that works
Face shield over safety glasses, boots, and gloves
Two hands on the wand; brace for kickback
No pressure washing from ladders; use a lift or extension wand
Barricade the area; protect windows, fixtures, and outlets

steps.name: Cleaners and runoff
hazards: Skin and eye contact with cleaners
controls: Read the SDS; gloves and goggles
Protect storm drains; contain wash water per local requirements

equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect before each use

competent_persons.note: Inspected by user before each use

steps.name: Access over stairs
hazards: Falls from ladders set on stairs
Falls over rails or down open sides
controls: Ladder levelers or stair-rated platforms; never an unsecured ladder on treads
Planks and platforms rated and secured
Keep stair guardrails in place

steps.name: Egress and other users
controls: Coordinate stair closure with the GC or building; keep one exit route open
Signs and barricades at each landing
Tape drop cloths down; keep tools off treads

steps.name: Lighting and ventilation
controls: Temporary lighting where needed
Ventilate at the top and bottom of the stair
Low-VOC products where possible; respirator per SDS

steps.name: Shafts and elevator pits
controls: No shaft or pit work without GC approval and the elevator locked out by the elevator contractor
Fall protection at every open shaft

equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect daily
Check daily

steps.name: Protect the public and property
steps.name_es: Proteger al público y la propiedad
controls: Barricade below overhead work; covered walkways where required
Move or cover vehicles in the drift zone
Protect windows, fixtures, and landscaping

steps.name: Control overspray in wind
controls: Check wind before spraying; stop when overspray drifts
Roll instead of spray near vehicles and occupied areas
Shields or screens where needed

steps.name: Work near overhead power lines
hazards: Electrocution from ladders, poles, or lifts
controls: Identify lines before setting up
Non-conductive ladders and poles
At least 10 ft clearance from lines

steps.name: Weather conditions
controls: Follow the heat illness template
Stop work in rain or high wind; wipe down wet surfaces before climbing
Sunscreen and brimmed hard hat attachments where helpful

equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect before use

Respirator type per the SDS; supplied-air or PAPR where required for isocyanates
Workers with prior sensitization reactions do not handle the product

steps.name: Mix two-component coatings

controls: Nitrile gloves and sleeves; goggles
Mix per the manufacturer ratio in a ventilated area
Mix only what can be applied within pot life; keep mixed pots out of the sun

steps.name: Apply coatings
controls: Respirator per the written program and SDS
Exhaust ventilation during application and cure
Keep other trades out of the area during application
Change gloves when contaminated; no skin contact with uncured material

steps.name: Control ignition sources
controls: No ignition sources in the area
Extinguisher staged; bond and ground containers
Explosion-proof fans and lights where solvent vapors are present

steps.name: Cure and restrict access
controls: Post the area until cured
Ventilate before re-occupancy per the manufacturer

steps.name: Repair cracks and joints

Safety glasses or goggles

steps.name: Apply primer and coating

Plan the pour to work toward the exit
Spiked shoes on wet coating

steps.name: Cure and restrict access

controls: Barricade and sign the area
Coordinate re-entry and traffic with the facility or GC

equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect before use; guards in place

Keep results on site

steps.name: Power tool cleaning (SSPC-SP 3)

Hearing protection
HEPA-shrouded tools where available
Guards in place; correct disc for the grinder speed

steps.name: Spray or roll overhead from a lift

controls: Follow the lift template
Goggles for overhead work
Rotate tasks and take stretch breaks

steps.name: Protect facility and equipment

controls: Mask and cover equipment below
Coordinate shutdowns with the facility; check wind outdoors

controls: Team lift or use carts for heavy pails
Mix at low speed; brace the mixer
Goggles and gloves per the SDS

steps.name: Spray heavy-build coatings
controls: Follow all airless controls; never point the gun at anyone
Respirator per the SDS; ventilate enclosed areas
Follow the lift template; tether tools

steps.name: Thickness checks and inspections
controls: Measure from the lift or scaffold only; never climb steel
Gloves when handling gauges on wet film
Coordinate third-party inspection hold points with the GC

controls: Initial exposure assessment and air monitoring
Interim protection per the task until the assessment is complete
Written compliance program on site

steps.name: Set up containment
hazards: Lead dust spreading to other areas
controls: Poly critical barriers; restrict access with warning signs
HEPA vacuums on hand before work starts
Cover floors and fixtures

steps.name: Wet scrape or HEPA sand
steps.name_es: Raspado húmedo o lijado con HEPA
controls: Wet methods and HEPA-shrouded tools only
No dry sweeping, dry sanding, or compressed air
Respirator per the exposure assessment

steps.name: Hygiene and decontamination
controls: No eating, drinking, or smoking in the work area
Wash hands and face before breaks and at the end of shift
Remove and bag coveralls at the exit

steps.name: Waste handling
controls: Bag, seal, and label waste per project requirements
Clean up with HEPA vacuum and wet wipe before removing containment

equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect hoses, guns, and guards daily

equipment_rows.training: Traffic control per the GC plan
equipment_rows.inspection: Check setup at start of shift

steps.name: Traffic control
controls: Follow the GC or owner traffic control plan
Cones, signs, and barricades before starting; Class 2 or 3 hi-vis
Flagger or spotter where traffic passes close
Face traffic when possible

steps.name: Operate the striper
controls: Follow airless controls for the striper gun
Check wind; protect nearby vehicles

steps.name: Materials and weather
controls: Read the SDS; gloves and eye protection
Follow the heat illness template

equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect guards and rollers before use
Blade disposal container on site

steps.name: Receive and stage rolls
hazards: Strains from heavy bolts and cartons
controls: Team lift heavy bolts; use carts and dollies
Store flat and off the floor, away from traffic
Keep pallets out of exits and aisles

steps.name: Prepare walls and apply primer
controls: Follow painting prep controls; HEPA cleanup
Safety glasses and gloves

steps.name: Paste and book
controls: Nitrile gloves
Wipe spills immediately; drop cloth at the paste table
Keep hands clear of pasting machine rollers; guards in place

steps.name: Hang drops
controls: Follow the ladder or scaffold template
Two installers on tall or heavy drops
Move the ladder instead of reaching

steps.name: Trim with blade and straightedge
controls: Fresh snap-off blades; cut away from the body
Cut-resistant gloves on the holding hand
Blades straight into a disposal container; never on the floor

equipment_rows.inspection: Inspect cord, hose, and plate before use; GFCI
Inspect before use

steps.name: Review existing substrate
hazards: Lead or asbestos in older buildings
controls: Confirm the hazardous materials survey before disturbing
Stop work and notify the PM if suspect material is found

steps.name: Score and apply remover
hazards: Skin and eye contact with remover
controls: Read the SDS; gloves and safety glasses
Guarded scoring tool; cut-resistant gloves

steps.name: Steam and strip
hazards: Burns from steam and hot plate
controls: Heat-resistant gloves; keep the plate moving and away from the body
GFCI on all cords; keep cords and connections out of water
Let the steamer cool before refilling

steps.name: Scrape and clean up
hazards: Slips on wet paper and paste
controls: Bag scraps as you go; wipe floors
Eye protection while scraping
